Everything here was built on 3 November 2026 from PubMed and PubMed Central (NCBI E-utilities) by the scripts in ../tools/, so it can be rebuilt or replaced. This page gives the full reference of the reference review and its limits; the other pages introduce it briefly as Pruna et al., J Clin Med 2026.

Doing the exercise? This page describes the reference review but does not list its decisions. The review itself (and ../answers/) names the included studies: open them only after step 3.

The reference review (PROVISIONAL)#

Pruna ED, Davidescu L, Sorop-Florea M, Demeter I, Iurciuc S, Varga NI, David VL, Buleu F, Horhat FG. Multimodal Hand Hygiene Interventions and Clinical Healthcare-Associated Infection Outcomes in Acute Care Hospitals: A Systematic Review of Quasi-Experimental Studies. J Clin Med 2026;15(10):3882. doi:10.3390/jcm15103882 · PMID 42194842 · PMCID PMC13207023 · CC BY 4.0 · PROSPERO CRD420261339769. Metadata and full text from PubMed / PubMed Central.

In short. A systematic review of quasi-experimental studies (interrupted time series, controlled and uncontrolled before-after) in acute care hospitals; 12 included studies; screening, extraction, risk of bias (ROBINS-I) and synthesis by two independent human reviewers without AI. Provisional: the workshop team may replace it (see How to replace).

Why this one (for now). Its question is exactly the exercise question; it is open access under CC BY, so its criteria, tables and included-study list can be reused here; its full text in PMC lists the 12 included studies (Table 1: characteristics; Table 2: outcomes) and the 21 studies excluded after full-text assessment; its criteria are explicit and demanding (hospital-wide or multi-ward scope, multimodal intervention, quasi-experimental designs only, clinical HAI outcome), which makes screening non-trivial. Two human reviewers screened, extracted and assessed risk of bias independently. Caveat: it is recent (2026), not a pre-generative-AI review. Its section 2.5 declares Rayyan (duplicate detection and screening workflow) and ChatGPT for English-language editing only, and states that no generative AI was used for selection, extraction, risk of bias or synthesis. This declaration is itself a useful example for the discussion on reporting AI use.

Alternatives considered (all verified in PubMed; DOIs from PubMed):

Review For Against
Gould DJ, Moralejo D, Drey N, Chudleigh JH, Taljaard M. Interventions to improve hand hygiene compliance in patient care. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2017;9:CD005186. doi:10.1002/14651858.CD005186.pub4, PMID 28862335 Cochrane methods, clearly conducted before generative AI (searches to October 2016), 26 studies, GRADE Primary outcome is compliance; only 8 studies report infection or colonisation. PMC holds the abstract only; the full text is not under CC BY, so tables cannot be shipped
Mouajou V, Adams K, DeLisle G, Quach C. Hand hygiene compliance in the prevention of hospital-acquired infections: a systematic review. J Hosp Infect 2022;119:33-48. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2021.09.016, PMID 34582962 Pre-generative-AI, directly about compliance and HAI incidence, 35 studies Closed access: the included-study list and tables cannot be checked or redistributed here
Zhang Y, Chen X, Lao Y, et al. Effects of the implementation of intelligent technology for hand hygiene in hospitals: systematic review and meta-analysis. J Med Internet Res 2023;25:e37249. doi:10.2196/37249, PMID 37247215 CC BY, searched to December 2022, 36 studies, meta-analysis of HAI rates Restricted to "intelligent technology" interventions (confusing in an AI workshop); study characteristics only in a supplement

Clancy C, Delungahawatta T, Dunne CP (J Hosp Infect 2021;111:6-26, doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2021.03.007) was also checked: CC BY and pre-AI, but it covers compliance trials without synthesising HAI outcomes.

What would make the reference authoritative. A review team's own records: (1) the export of the original title/abstract screening (one row per record with PMID and include/exclude), which turns the gold standard into real title/abstract decisions (see "How to replace" below); (2) the review's own extraction sheet, to replace the provisional extraction values; (3) confirmation of the included-study list. If the workshop team adopts another review (for example one of its own reviews conducted without AI), the same three files are needed.

Screening set: screening_records.csv (60 records)#

Columns: record_id,pmid,doi,title,abstract,year,journal,license. Order shuffled with a fixed seed (2026); record_id R001-R060. The answers are in ../answers/screening_gold.csv (record_id,gold_decision,gold_basis), built from ../answers/reference_key.yaml.

Part n Reference decision Source
Studies included by the reference review 12 include its Table 1 and reference list (refs 35-46)
Studies excluded by the review after full-text assessment 21 exclude its Results section (refs 14-34; reasons in its Supplementary File S2). They passed the review's title/abstract stage
Near misses from an approximate PubMed search 26 exclude not included in the review; chosen by the workshop team because they fail a criterion clearly: single ICU/NICU or single ward (5), process outcomes only (7), randomised trials (3), long-term care (1), broad infection-control bundles (5), reviews (2), veterinary (1), outbreak report (1), ecological study (1)
Possible gold-standard error 1 exclude a well-known hospital-wide programme that appears to meet the criteria but is neither included nor listed among the review's full-text exclusions; kept as a discussion item

Approximate search (PubMed, 3 November 2026; full strings in ../review_config.yaml): the review's four domains (hand hygiene AND healthcare-associated infection AND quasi-experimental design AND hospital, English, NOT long-term care) returned 367 records and retrieves 8 of the 12 included studies; a second query (randomised trials, ICU-only, long-term care, reviews) supplied the remaining near-miss types.

Abstracts and licences. An abstract is shipped only when the article's PubMed Central licence is CC BY or CC0 (17 records; text © the authors, copied verbatim from PubMed, source identified by the pmid and doi columns). For the other 43 the abstract column is empty and license says why. They can be filled on your own computer, not redistributed:

Terminal
python3 activity/tools/fetch_abstracts.py        # -> activity/data/local/screening_records_full.csv (git-ignored)

The records page does the same in the browser for chat users.

Limits (say them in the debrief).

  • The reference decision is the review's final inclusion, not its title/abstract decision. At title/abstract stage the 21 full-text exclusions were includes; score_screening.py therefore also shows a "title/abstract-stage view".

  • The review screened a fairly small set (353 records at title/abstract stage) from a narrower search than the one used here. Eligible-looking studies exist that it did not include (one is flagged in the set). Near misses were chosen so that their exclusion does not depend on this: each fails a criterion on its own. The workshop team's reasons are notes, not the review's.

  • The review's Table 1 lists "Larson et al., 2010" while the cited paper (PMID 10971880) was published in 2000.

  • Records are not a random sample of a real search: includes are over-represented (20%) to make 30 minutes useful.

Extraction set: papers.csv, extraction_form.csv, fulltext/#

Three of the 12 included studies, chosen because they are open access in PMC and differ in length and difficulty:

study_id Paper Licence Full text here
Phan2020 Antimicrob Resist Infect Control 2020;9:51, doi:10.1186/s13756-020-00712-x, PMID 32276646 CC BY 4.0 fulltext/Phan2020.txt
Mestre2012 PLoS One 2012;7(10):e47200, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0047200, PMID 23110061 CC BY 4.0 fulltext/Mestre2012.txt
AlKuwaiti2017 Interv Med Appl Sci 2017;9(3):137-143, doi:10.1556/1646.9.2017.24, PMID 29201437 CC BY-NC 3.0 not shipped: python3 activity/tools/fetch_fulltext.py

The form (extraction_form.csv: field,definition,allowed_values,type,core) follows the data items the reference review says it extracted (country, setting, design, wards, intervention, periods, comparator, outcome definitions, denominators, findings, compliance, co-interventions), plus effect estimate and direction.

The reference values (../answers/extraction_gold.csv: study_id,field,value,source_quote,location,review_table_value,notes) are provisional: prepared by the workshop team from the full texts, every value with a verbatim quote that build_extraction_gold.py check finds in the text, and cross-checked with the reference review's own tables (review_table_value, copied verbatim; all tables of the review for all 12 studies are in ../answers/reference_review_tables.csv). They must be validated against the review team's extraction sheet before being called a gold standard. Where the paper contradicts itself, or the review's table differs from the paper, the notes column says so.

How to replace the reference review#

  1. Edit ../review_config.yaml (citation, PICO, criteria C1-Cn, PMC ID) and ../answers/reference_key.yaml (PMIDs of included studies, full-text exclusions, near misses with reasons).

  2. Rebuild the screening set: python3 activity/tools/build_screening_set.py (--dry-run to preview). With the review team's own screening export (CSV with a PMID column and a decision column): python3 activity/tools/build_screening_set.py --from-export export.csv --id-col pmid --decision-col decision.

  3. Extraction: update papers.csv, run python3 activity/tools/fetch_fulltext.py, python3 activity/tools/build_extraction_gold.py tables (review tables) and python3 activity/tools/build_extraction_gold.py skeleton --out my_work/gold_skeleton.csv, fill values and quotes, then python3 activity/tools/build_extraction_gold.py check --write.

  4. Update the criteria table in ../README.md and the short mentions of the review ("Pruna et al.") in the repository's README.md, activity/README.md, activity/quick_card.md, beginners/README.md and docs/index.html, then run python3 docs/sync_data.py for the website.
